name: Software in the Public Interest
summary: US charity that holds donations and assets, and signs contracts, for established open source software and hardware projects, which stay independent.

evidence.quote: founded to act as a fiscal sponsor for organizations that develop open source software and hardware
founded to act as a fiscal sponsor for organizations that develop open source software and hardware
is a non-profit corporation registered in the state of New York

projects.value: Open source software and hardware projects that are substantial and significant

evidence.quote: founded to act as a fiscal sponsor for organizations that develop open source software and hardware. Our mission is to help substantial and significant open source projects

gate.value: Judged on an established developer community and broad use

evidence.quote: Does the project have an established development community, history of software releases, etc? Significance: Is the project used by a broad audience, or does it have political or market significance?

fees.value: No cost to become or stay a project

evidence.quote: There is no cost to become or remain an associated project.

value.note: Its pages describe accepting donations and holding funds; they don’t say who applies for grants.

evidence.quote: SPI will accept donations and hold funds on behalf of associated projects.

conditions.value: Money it holds can move only to another US 501(c)(3)

evidence.quote: Once held by SPI, funds may only be transferred to another 501(c)3 US non-profit with a compatible purpose.

conditions.value: It owns equipment over $300 bought with its funds

evidence.quote: Substantial equipment, software or other assets valued at over $300 which an associated project purchases with SPI funds are owned by SPI.
SPI does not assist with fundraising activities.
all contracts MUST be signed by an officer of SPI unless the board explicitly authorizes another entity to sign a contract

steps.value: Contact the board for an informal talk

evidence.quote: Projects interested in becoming SPI associated projects are welcome to contact the board for a discreet informal discussion on whether the project is likely to be accepted as an associated project.

steps.value: If a board member finds the project suitable, they may agree to sponsor the application

evidence.quote: If a board member is personally satisfied that the project is suitable for associated project status they may agree to sponsor the project's application.

steps.value: Formal application, sent to that board member

evidence.quote: If the project wishes to proceed, a formal application is sent to the sponsor.

steps.value: Discussion, then it may go to a vote at a board meeting, held monthly

evidence.quote: After sufficient time for discussion (normally at least three days), the resolution may be submitted for a vote at an SPI board meeting. These meetings are public and held monthly

form_asks.value: Project details, the services needed and a liaison

evidence.quote: The name and details of the project Which SPI services will be needed Who is going to be the liaison to SPI
If the project already has existing contracts, liabilities or pending litigations, they must also disclose their existence to SPI.
